WISER, the new semantic search engine we present in this paper, outperforms all other competitors in the task of expert finding in academia, and that it is suitable for technology transfer in our university, and in general, for all the other universities that have the same needs.

(1) we have built a semantic search engine for academic expert finding; (2) our engine jointly combines classical language modelling techniques with the Wikipedia knowledge graph via entity linking; (3) it is able to index and profile the whole research community of the University of PISA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following main contributions: (i) a new semantic approach for expert finding, based on the use of entity linking and entity embeddings; (ii) a novel graph based profiling technique, which models the expertise of each academic author with a small, labelled and weighted graph drawn by Wikipedia; (iii) a new set of profile centred strategies for scoring the experts, which exploit the semantic relatedness of author's profile and query topic via the graph of expertise.

the development of novel approaches for expert finding in Academia, based on semantic techniques, and on the use of these approaches for the management and the exploitation of the research community of our University.

the design and development of a novel semantic search engine which is able to retrieve the most relevant authors in a given research field by jointly exploiting both text and knowledge based approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

WISER represents an innovative approach to semantic search for expert finding in the academia, which is based on the joint exploitation of classical language modeling techniques and the Wikipedia Knowledge Graph.
WISER is a novel semantic search engine which combines the advantages of classic document centric techniques with a new set of profile centrid approaches based on the Wikipedia Knowledge Graph.

our approach is a promising solution for expert finding, and that the semantic graph of expertise that we propose for modelling the author's profile is an effective and novel way of representing author's knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

WISER can be used to build an effective and efficient semantic search engine for academic expertise finding, thus helping the research community to identify the best experts in a given research topic, and to foster technology transfer in Universities.

, in order to improve the effectiveness of expert finding, one has to combine classical language modeling techniques with semantic relatedness functions, and to model author's expertise with a small and labeled graph drawn from Wikipedia, via a suitable profiling technique.

WISER is a novel, effective and scalable system for finding experts in academia which combines the power of language modeling techniques and the wealth of information available in the Wikipedia Knowledge Graph.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, by exploiting a proper semantic representation of authors' expertise, we are able to improve the quality of expert finding systems in academia, thus making them more useful in technology transfer and other similar activities.

, by exploiting the semantic relatedness of Wikipedia entities, we can effectively and efficiently model the expertise of each researcher and, in this way, we can support the expert finding task, which is a fundamental step in the technology transfer process.

, by exploiting the knowledge graph of Wikipedia, it is possible to model and profile the experts in a given community, and thus build a semantic search engine for finding experts, which is both effective and scalable.
